questions.stem: All of the following structures pass through the esophageal hiatus except

options.label: B
options.text: Esophageal branches of the left gastric vessels

questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (D) Thoracic duct Exp: Thoracic duct passes through aortic opening

questions.stem: A 29 year-old man comes in with a stab wound, cannot raise his arm above horizontal, and exhibits a condition known as winged scapula while pushing against the wall. Which of the following structures of the brachial plexus would most likely be damaged?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (D) Roots Exp: winged scapula while pushing against the wall means patient has S. Anterior muscle paralyzed because of Long Thoracic nerve involvement which arises from roots.

questions.stem: The middle radioulnar joint is a :
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) Syndesmosis Ref:Read the text below Sol: FIBROUS JOINTS Are joined by fibrous tissue. Are of three types - a) SYNDESMOSIS - the bones are connected by interosseous ligament. - eg. inferior tibiofibular joint, Intervertebral joints b) SUTURES :Peculiar to skull & are immovable c) GOMPHOSIS :is a peg & socket joint , eg. Tooth & socket joint

questions.stem: A football player experiences an anterior dislocation of the shoulder. Cutaneous sensation over the lower half of the deltoid muscle is impaired. These findings suggest damage to which of the following nerves?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (A) Axillary Ref: Read the text below Sol: The axillary nerve can be damaged during anterior dislocation of the shoulder, causing loss of sensation in the skin overlying the lower half of the deltoid muscle.

questions.stem: The musculophrenic arteries give rise to ?

options.label: A
options.text: Anterior intercostal arteries for intercostals spaces 7–9

options.label: B
options.text: Posterior intercostals arteries for intercostals spaces 3–11

questions.answerText: Anterior intercostal arteries for intercostals spaces 7–9
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (A) Anterior intercostal arteries for intercostals spaces 7–9 Reference – Read the text below Sol: • The musculophrenic artery gives rise to anterior intercostal arteries for intercostal spaces 7–9.

questions.stem: The clavipectoral fascia is pierced by which of the following structures?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) Lateral pectoral nerve Ref.:Read the text below Sol : Structures Piercing Clavipectoral Fascia :  Lateral pectoral nerve  Cephalic vein  Thoracoacromial vessels  Lymphatics passing from breast & pectoral region to the apical group of axillary lymph nodes.

questions.stem: Anterior belly of digastric is a derivate of :
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (A) 1st branchial arch Ref: Read the text below Sol Anterior belly of digastric is derived from first arch Posterior belly of digastric is derived from Second arch

questions.stem: Epithelial lining of esophagus is :
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) Stratified squamous non- keratinized Ref: Read the text below Sol esophagus is lined by Stratified squamous non- keratinized

questions.stem: Which part of the ear has origin from all the three layer of germ layer :
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) Tympanic membrane Ref: Read the text below Sol Tympanic membrane has origin from all the three layer of germ layer

questions.stem: The Left superior intercostal vein drains into :
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) Left brachiocephalic vein Ref– Read the text below Sol: • The 1st left posterior intercostal vein drains into the left brachiocephalic vein. • The 2nd , 3rd , & 4th left posterior intercostal veins join to form the left superior intercostals vein that drains into the left brachiocephalic vein. • The 5th , 6th, 7th& 8th join to form the accessory hemiazygous vein which drain in the azygous vein • The 9th, 10th , 11th& 12th join to form the hemiazygous vein which also drain into the azygous vein.

questions.stem: False regarding Erb’s paralysis?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) Difficulty in abduction Ref: Read the text below Sol : Adducted and medial rotated arm, flexed and pronated forearm is seen in Erb’s paralysis

questions.stem: Tensor Tympani is supplied by
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) Trigeminal Ref: Langman's Medical Embryology 10thed pg 258

questions.stem: Which of the following muscle is supplied by a branch of Posterior cord of brachial plexus :
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (A) Teres minor Ref: Read the text below Sol : Posterior cord gives five branches, including axillary nerve which supplies teres minor muscle.

questions.stem: Spinal part of accessory nerve supplies :
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) Sternocleidomastoid Exp: Spinal Accessory nerve supplies SCM & Trapezius

questions.stem: Soft palate muscles are supplied by:
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (A) . VAC • Most of the palate muscles are supplied by the vagus accessory complex ( pharyngeal plexus), except tensor palati (which is supplied by the mandibular nerve, trigeminal).

questions.stemHtml: Which nerve supplies the marked area
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) Radial nerve

questions.stem: Clavipectoral fascia splits to enclose subclavius and pectoralis minor, and continues as:
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (D) Suspensory ligament Ref: Read the text below Sol : • Below pectoralis minor muscle, clavipetoral fascia extends downwards as the suspensory ligament of axilla, which attach and pulls up the dome of the axillary fascia (and maintain the concavity of the axilla).

questions.stem: Foot drop occurs as a result of injury to:
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) Deep peroneal nerve Ref: Read the text below Sol : • The common peroneal nerve divides into superficial peroneal ( lateral compartment) & a deep peroneal ( anterior compartment) • The muscles of the anterior compartment cause dorsiflexion at the ankle joint. • Paralysis thus results in foot drop. • The gait in cases of foot drop is High Stepping Gait.

questions.stemHtml: Artery beneath red mark in the image below.
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (A) Middle meningeal • The pterion is the region where the frontal, parietal, temporal, and sphenoid bone join together. • Anterior division of middle meningeal artery overlies it • It is located on the side of the skull, just behind the temple.

questions.stem: Brachialis is supplied by -
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) Radial and musculocutaneous nerve Ref: Read the text below Sol Brachialis is supplied by Radial and musculocutaneous nerve

questions.stem: Killian dehiscence is in:
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) Inferior constrictor • Inferior constrictor muscle has two parts: Upper thyropharyngeus made up of oblique fibres and lower cricopharyngeus made up of transverse fibres. • There is a potential gap posteriorly between the two parts called as pharyngeal dimple or Killian’s dehiscence.

questions.stem: Cells which surround the oocyte in Graffian follicle are called?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) cumulus Oophorus Exp: Cells which surround the oocyte in Graffian follicle are called cumulus Oophorus and site of attachment is called Discus Proligerus.

questions.stem: Epiploic Foramen is bounded by all except
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) Free border of Greater omentum

questions.stem: Which of the following is taking origin from Infraglenoid tubercle :
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) Long head of triceps Ref.: Read the text below Sol : Long head of triceps Origin : Infraglenoid tubercle Insertion : With other heads of Triceps olecranon process

questions.stem: The nucleus that gives rise to motor fibers that innervate muscles of larynx, pharynx, and palate is the:-

options.label: D
options.text: Dorsal motor nucleus of the vagus

questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) Nucleus ambiguus Ref: Read the text below Sol : • The nucleus ambiguus gives rise to the motor innervation of larynx, pharynx, and palate. The hypoglossal nucleus innervates the tongue muscle.

questions.stem: Froment test is positive in lesion of :
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) Ulnar nerve Ref: Read the text below Sol It is seen in paralysis of Adductor policis supplied by ulnar nerve

questions.stem: Which of the following is the first germ layer to be formed :
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) Endoderm Ref: Read the text below Sol: Endoderm is the first germ layer to be formed

questions.stem: Flexion of MCP joint and extension of IP joints is the major action of All except:
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (D) FDS Ref: Read the text below Sol Flexion of MCP joint and extension of IP joints is the major action of Lumbricals & interossei . FDS flexes the Proximal interphalangeal joint

questions.stem: All of the following statements correctly apply to a bronchopulmonary segment except

options.label: A
options.text: It is separated from adjacent segments by connective tissue septa.

options.label: B
options.text: It is the largest subdivision of a lobe.

options.label: D
options.text: It is named according to the segmental bronchus supplying it.

questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) It is not resectable. Reference – Read the text below Sol: • A bronchopulmonary segment is a pyramid shaped segment of the lung with its apex facing the lung root and its base at the pleural surface. • It is the largest subdivision of a lobe and is separated from adjacent segments by connective tissue. It is surgically resectable

questions.stem: Left ovarian vein drain into :
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) Left renal vein Ref: Read the text below Sol Left ovarian vein drains into Left renal vein right ovarian vein drains to IVC

questions.stem: A 46-year-old man complains of dryness of the mouth. On examination he lack salivary secretion from the submandibular gland. This indicates a lesion of which of the following nervous structures?

options.label: B
options.text: Chorda tympani in the middle ear cavity

questions.answerText: Chorda tympani in the middle ear cavity
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) Chorda tympani in the middle ear cavity Ref: Read the text below Sol Because Chorda tympani in the middle ear cavity carries the salivatory fibers to Submandibular gland

questions.stem: Capacitation takes place mainly in :-
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (D) Fallopian tube Ref: Read the text below Sol : Fallopian tube contributes most among female genital tract Although all parts as given in options are involved in this process

questions.stemHtml: A young patient with absent thymus and presented with hypoparathyroidism and tetany. Which of the following marked area in the picture is defective in this condition?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (A) Ref: Read the text below Sol : Given condition is Digeorge syndrome. “A” is the marked area for third pharyngeal pouch from where thymus and inf. Parathyroid develop

questions.stem: Arterial supply of caecum is through :
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) Ileocolic artery Ref: Read the text below Sol Ileocolic artery supplies terminal part of ileum , part of Ascending colon,Caecum and appendix

questions.stem: A middle-aged women complained that her right-hand tremors when she attempts to insert a thread in the eye of sewing needle; and her body sways towards the right side while walking. On physical examination the Physician found that: there is flaccidity of limb muscles on the right side, and when she was asked to touch the tip of her nose with her right index finger, the finger tended to overshoot the target. Which part of the Brain is affected?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) Cerebellum Ref: Read the text below Sol All the given features indicate Cerebellar syndrome

questions.stem: A patient recovering from a traumatic injury to the face now finds himself unable to chew his food. On physical examination, his jaw deviates to the right side. The nerve that has been injured in this patient exits the skull through which of the following foramina?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) Foramen ovale Ref: Read the text below Sol All the given features indicate that Mandibular nerve is involved hence Foramen ovale is correct

questions.stem: Which of the following artery is present in anatomical snuff box :
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) Radial artery Ref: Snell’s Clinical Anatomy, 7th ed ., p-533

questions.stem: Positive Trendelenburg sign indicates of which group of gluteus muscles :

options.label: D
options.text: Gluteus Maximus, Gluteus Medius and Gluteus Minimus

questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (A) Gluterus Medius and Gluteus Minimus Ref: Read the text below Sol This is done to check the integrity of Gluterus Medius and Gluteus Minimus and their nerve supply ie superior gluteal nerve.

questions.stem: A Patient presents with congenital diaphragmatic hernia which is located in posterior lateral position. Which of the following structure is most likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (A) Bochdalek Hernia Ref: Read the text below Sol Bochdalek Hernia is Most common congenital diaphragmatic hernia which is located in posterior lateral position.
